IX.  THE  SEPARATE  FUNCTION  OF  THE  EODS 
AND  THE  CONES.  Interest  in  the  phenomena 
of  visual  sensation  has  centred  of  late  years  in 
the  question  of  the  discrimination  of  function 
of  rods  and  cones,  and  in  questions  intimately 
connected  with  it.  It  would  be  singular  if 
organs  of  such  very  distinctive  structure 
(knob-like  or  finger-like;  connections  with 
the  bipolar  cells,  Fig.  6),  and  of  such  very 
different  chemical  contents  (presence  or  ab 
sence  of  the  rod-pigment),  should  not  play 
a  different  rule  in  the  visual  economy. 
Neither  of  these  objective  differences  was 
known  at  the  time  when  Max  Schultze  first 
made  the  suggestion  that  the  rods  constitute 
an  organ  for  black  and  white  vision  only,  and 
that  colour  is  mediated  only  by  the 'cones 
(1866);  but  there  was  already  sufficient 
ground  for  his  view  in  the  fact  that  in  the
